sections.heading: C2 — Seat adjustment and occupant protection
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Seat adjustment and occupant protection

FACT_ID: sec04-R01 | anchor: A01
The listed seatbelt-law exceptions include vehicles manufactured before January 1, 1968. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-R02 | anchor: A01
An occupant unable to wear a belt for medical reasons needs to carry a physician’s written statement to use the stated exemption. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-R03 | anchor: A01
The stated special-mobile-equipment seatbelt exemption applies to the operator of a vehicle licensed in that category. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-R04 | anchor: A01
Special mobile equipment is not primarily designed or used to transport people or property and is moved on highways only incidentally. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-R05 | anchor: A01
A driver making frequent stops as part of official job duties may receive a seatbelt exemption from the Department of Justice. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-R06 | anchor: A01
The handbook points frequent-stop workers to exemption form MVD-SE1. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-R07 | anchor: A01
Booster seats are recommended for older children until the lap-and-shoulder belt fits them properly. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-R08 | anchor: A01
A proper adult-belt fit for a child is usually reached at about four feet nine inches of height. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-R09 | anchor: A01
If a child must sit in the front of an airbag-equipped vehicle, use a child safety seat with the vehicle belt or a booster with the lap-and-shoulder belt. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-R10 | anchor: A01
When a child must ride in front, move the seat as far back from the active airbag as possible. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-R11 | anchor: A01
Never put a rear-facing child seat in a front passenger position with an active airbag. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-R12 | anchor: A01
Whenever possible, children younger than 13 should be restrained in the back seat. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-R13 | anchor: A01
Every passenger needs an independent, properly used belt or child restraint. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-R14 | anchor: A01
Holding a child while riding can result in crushing the child during a collision. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0030]
